task: Create original Figma website template from TASE travel ticket reference

styleDNA.typographyBehavior: Friendly large travel headline, calm dark-green hierarchy, compact route metadata, and rounded ticket labels.
styleDNA.layoutRhythm: Airy planner opening, route scan, timeline proof, scenic pause, fare decision, reassurance, pricing, FAQ, and booking closure.
styleDNA.spacingDensity: Generous travel spacing with broad off-white fields and denser fare comparison only where decisions need it.
styleDNA.colorBehavior: Light neutral base with forest booking action, sky route accents, and pale sage support bands.
styleDNA.imageDirection: Destination, route map, station, boarding pass, support app, and profile zones stay as editable placeholders.
styleDNA.shapeLanguage: Rounded ticket cards, soft planner boards, pill chips, fare cards, and checklist rows.
styleDNA.effectLanguage: Soft card shadows, selected fare border, route-line accents, and restrained surface separation.
styleDNA.premiumSignal: Feels like a paid travel-ticket template because it includes route search, cards, process, fare, support, proof, packages, FAQ, CTA, and DS coverage.

referenceStandard.observedSectionCountRange: Travel ticket references need a full booking journey; 9-12 sections are commercially appropriate.
referenceStandard.sectionRoleEvidence: The reference implies travel route selection, trust, booking flow, destination proof, fare confidence, and support.
referenceStandard.layoutShapeInventory: Light hero planner, ticket cards, route grids, rounded media panels, pricing modules, FAQ, and footer.
referenceStandard.colorRoleInventory: Reference suggests green booking action and airy travel surfaces; the rebuild expands this into forest, sage, sky, warm destination, and deep fare roles.
referenceStandard.effectGradientInventory: Soft surfaces and rounded ticket depth are more important than heavy decorative effects.
referenceStandard.marketplaceCompletenessClues: A sellable ticket template needs route search, fare comparison, support assurances, traveler proof, packages, placeholders, and a design-system board.
referenceStandard.remixPlan: Keep the commercial travel-ticket logic but rebuild the flow as RoamPass with different hero grammar, fare band, proof wall, package pricing, and source hygiene.

designIntentLock.targetBuyer: Marketplace buyer building bus, train, ferry, flight, or multi-route ticket booking websites.
designIntentLock.useCase: Complete homepage source with travel booking sections, placeholder media, and a separate design-system board.
designIntentLock.marketplaceValue: Gives buyers a useful travel-ticket product flow instead of a generic travel landing page.
designIntentLock.primaryGoal: Make travelers compare routes, understand booking steps, trust support, and choose a ticket package.

visualGrammar.gridBehavior: 12-column airy travel container with planner board, route grids, timeline, panorama, fare band, and support cards.
visualGrammar.spacingCadence: Relaxed 88-120px rhythm with a dense fare-comparison decision pause.
visualGrammar.typeHierarchy: Optimistic display headline, calm h2 sections, compact route metadata, and clear CTA labels.
visualGrammar.surfaceDepth: White ticket cards, pale sage surfaces, soft shadows, and selected fare treatments.
visualGrammar.colorRoles: Off-white base, white cards, forest CTA, sky route accent, warm destination cue, deep green fare band.
visualGrammar.imageTreatment: Destination, map, station, boarding pass, support, and profile placeholders remain text-based and editable.
visualGrammar.effectLogic: Effects communicate booking confidence, route clarity, and selected fare emphasis.
visualGrammar.componentRhythm: Route cards, timeline steps, panorama, fare cards, support cards, testimonials, and packages alternate in purpose.

referenceBoundary.allowedToLearn: Travel-ticket purpose, booking confidence, green CTA role, airy trust tone, and marketplace completeness.
referenceBoundary.forbiddenToCopy: Do not copy exact layout, color palette, section order, hero grammar, component scaffold, imagery, logo, or ticket-card cadence.

colorRoleRemapping.referenceDominantColorIdentity: bright travel-ticket page with green booking emphasis
colorRoleRemapping.referenceColorRoles: light background, green action, supportive travel imagery, and calm text
colorRoleRemapping.remappedPaletteDirection: off-white, forest green, pale sage, sky route accent, warm destination cue, and deep fare band
colorRoleRemapping.newAccentIdentity: sky route accent and warm destination cue make the template distinct while forest remains the booking signal
colorRoleRemapping.preservedEmotionalRole: Trust, ease, route clarity, and booking confidence are preserved.
colorRoleRemapping.avoidedExactHues: The palette is role-remapped and avoids sampling the provided travel reference directly.
colorRoleRemapping.contrastHierarchyBehavior: Green marks primary booking choices, sky marks navigation/route cues, and deep green isolates fare decisions.

visualMoodReinterpretation.reinterpretedMood: Confident route-planner product with calm ticket selection and support assurance.
visualMoodReinterpretation.changedComposition: The design uses a planner board, route catalog, timeline, panorama, and fare band rather than the reference composition.
visualMoodReinterpretation.changedHierarchy: Fare comparison, support assurance, and traveler proof have larger decision roles.
visualMoodReinterpretation.changedAssetTreatment: Travel media is represented through editable text clue placeholders.
visualMoodReinterpretation.changedDepthEffect: Soft card depth and selected fare surfaces replace any direct reference visual treatment.

structuralReconfiguration.referenceStructurePattern: Travel ticket homepage with booking hero, route/product cards, trust, pricing, and support.
structuralReconfiguration.newStructurePattern: Route-planner journey with 12 sections: hero, trust strip, route tickets, timeline, panorama, fare comparison, support, proof, packages, FAQ, CTA, footer.
structuralReconfiguration.heroGrammarChange: Hero becomes a route-planner board with ticket search form and map/support placeholder.
structuralReconfiguration.sectionOrderChange: Route selection, process, destination proof, fare comparison, support, proof, and packages form a new booking journey.
structuralReconfiguration.gridSystemChange: Uses airy route grids, timeline spine, panorama, and fare band instead of dark console rows or a generic card grid.
structuralReconfiguration.ctaFlowChange: CTAs move from book route to selected fare to final ticket-pass action.
structuralReconfiguration.componentLayoutChange: Components become planner form, route cards, timeline steps, fare cards, support cards, testimonials, packages, and checklist FAQ.

patternDivergence.divergenceFromReference: Original naming, planner structure, fare band, proof wall, package logic, and placeholder treatment.
patternDivergence.divergenceFromPreviousTemplate: Avoids KineticCast's dark broadcast hero, red signal rail, match ledger, replay studio, fan rooms, and red CTA closure.
patternDivergence.heroDivergence: Bright route planner and map placeholder replace broadcast console grammar.
patternDivergence.sectionRhythmDivergence: Airy travel pauses, panorama, timeline, and fare decision band replace dense sports streaming rhythm.
patternDivergence.visualLanguageDivergence: Forest, sage, sky, warm destination, and off-white travel roles replace graphite, red, and oxblood.
patternDivergence.componentCadenceDivergence: Route tickets, booking steps, fare cards, support assurances, and traveler proof replace event rows and sports cards.

sectionLogic.roleOfEachSection: Hero starts route search; trust strip lowers risk; route cards show supply; timeline explains booking; panorama creates desire; fare comparison supports choice; support, proof, packages, FAQ, CTA, and footer close buyer concerns.
sectionLogic.buyerJourneyFlow: Search intent, route confidence, process clarity, destination desire, price choice, reassurance, social proof, package decision, and final booking action.
sectionLogic.fillerSectionsRemoved: No generic feature strip; every section maps to travel-ticket buyer utility.
sectionLogic.productFamilyDepthStandard: Full travel ticket marketplace templates need search, routes, process, destination, fare, support, proof, packages, and FAQ, so 12 sections are justified.

marketplaceReadiness.sectionDepth: 12 meaningful homepage sections with travel-ticket specific modules.
marketplaceReadiness.premiumSignal: Airy planner presentation, route cards, fare band, proof wall, and design-system documentation.
marketplaceReadiness.editability: Named Figma sections, editable text, source placeholders, and auto-layout modules.
marketplaceReadiness.sourceReadiness: Separate design-system board, placeholder policy, token receipt, pack overview, and visual screenshots are present.
marketplaceReadiness.previewValue: Pack overview and homepage screenshot make the template understandable as a travel-ticket product.
marketplaceReadiness.commercialUsefulness: Useful for buses, trains, ferries, flights, and multi-route ticketing startups.
marketplaceReadiness.nonGenericProof: Contains planner board, route catalog, booking timeline, fare comparison, insurance/support cards, traveler proof, and travel package pricing.
